content.en:
When a boat travels in flowing water (current/stream):
• Let speed of boat in still water = u km/h, and speed of stream = v km/h.
• Downstream (along the current): Stream aids the boat → Effective speed D = u + v.
• Upstream (against the current): Stream opposes the boat → Effective speed U = u - v.
• Speed of boat in still water: u = (D + U) / 2.
• Speed of stream / current: v = (D - U) / 2.
• Average speed for a round trip (equal distance d): Average Speed = (2 * D * U) / (D + U) = (u² - v²) / u.

content.en: Downstream Speed (D) = u + v | Upstream Speed (U) = u - v | Boat Speed in Still Water (u) = (D + U)/2 | Stream Speed (v) = (D - U)/2
content.hi: Downstream Speed (D) = u + v | Upstream Speed (U) = u - v | Boat Speed in Still Water (u) = (D + U)/2 | Stream Speed (v) = (D - U)/2

content.en:
Illustrative Problem: A man rows a boat downstream at 15 km/h and upstream at 9 km/h. Find the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the stream.
Solution:
• Speed in still water: u = (15 + 9)/2 = 24/2 = 12 km/h.
• Speed of stream: v = (15 - 9)/2 = 6/2 = 3 km/h.

question.en: A motorboat can travel at 10 km/h in still water. It traveled 91 km downstream and then returned to the same starting point. If the round trip took a total of 20 hours, what is the speed of the river current?
question.hi: A motorboat can travel at 10 km/h in still water. It traveled 91 km downstream and then returned to the same starting point. If the round trip took a total of 20 hours, what is the speed of the river current?

explanation.en: Let river speed be v km/h. Downstream time = 91 / (10 + v). Upstream time = 91 / (10 - v). Total time = 91/(10+v) + 91/(10-v) = 20. 91 * [ (10-v) + (10+v) ] / (100 - v²) = 20 => 91 * 20 / (100 - v²) = 20 => 91 = 100 - v² => v² = 9 => v = 3 km/h.
